study: Metric relationship and comparator-ladder order (audit F3, M01, M02, M03)

criteria.R2_beta_derivation: log10(R2_MAX_WIDTH_FACTOR) = 0.301 of one decade, the granularity of the ratio claim (ADR-0040 s1.1); the same fraction of the 1.0 index unit the four design-level dbeta values span (0.90 to 1.87) gives 0.30

constant_B_family.verdict: one value of B carries a whole range of dbeta, so there is no map from B alone

restricted_monotonicity.statement: with EITHER absolute branch probability held fixed, dbeta is a strictly increasing function of B

two_notions_of_common_mode.verdict: cancellation in B and cancellation in dbeta are different conditions and neither implies the other

tail_asymptotics.statement: for small p, dbeta ~ ln(B) / beta, so at fixed B dbeta shrinks as the tail deepens

m_p.channel_reading: common-mode: multiplies the single-source H_c in both branches

l_c_lower.channel_reading: transient-only: no static channel at all

l_c_upper.channel_reading: transient-only: no static channel at all

R1.estimand: the transient failure COUNT at the level
R1.reason: both estimators are functions of the same two counts on the same rows, so a count floor governs both; this is the shared sample, not a map between metrics

R2.estimand: the multiplicative width of the 95 per cent interval on B
R2.reason: a width condition on a ratio has no image in index space; see metric_relationship.R2_width_does_not_transfer

R2_beta.estimand: the additive width of the directly evaluated 95 per cent paired-bootstrap interval on delta beta
R2_beta.derivation: log10(R2_MAX_WIDTH_FACTOR) = 0.301 of one decade, the granularity of the ratio claim (ADR-0040 s1.1); the same fraction of the 1.0 index unit the four design-level dbeta values span (0.90 to 1.87) gives 0.30
